blocks.text: **The problem.** Given an `m × n` grid of non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left to the bottom-right, moving only **right or down**, that **minimises the sum** of the numbers on it. Return that sum.

blocks.alt: The grid 1 3 1 / 1 5 1 / 4 2 1 and its table of cheapest sums: 1 4 5 / 2 7 6 / 6 8 7. Each cell adds its own number to the cheaper of the cell above and the cell to the left; 6 = 1 + min(5, 7). The cheapest path, 1 3 1 1 1, costs 7.

elements.text: best[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(best above, best on the left)
elements.originalText: best[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(best above, best on the left)

blocks.text: The idea: the cheaper way in

Let `best[r][c]` be the cheapest sum of a path from the start to `(r, c)`, including both ends. The last step came from above or from the left, so `best[r][c] = grid[r][c] + min(best[r−1][c], best[r][c−1])`. Along the top row and the left column there's only one way in. It's Unique Paths with `min` and `+` instead of `+`.
**Time O(m · n), space O(m · n).** Off-grid cells return infinity so `min` never picks them — but `INT_MAX + grid[r][c]` would overflow, which is why the start is handled before reaching them.

blocks.caption: Each cell adds its own cost to the cheaper of the cells above and to the left.

blocks.text: **Time O(m · n), space O(n).** Starting the row at infinity (except `row[0]`) makes the first row only take values from the left.

blocks.alt: Memoized recursion: O(m · n) time, O(m · n) space. Table: O(m · n) time, O(m · n) space. One row: O(m · n) time, O(n) space.

items: **One row or column** — the sum of everything.
**Zeros** — free cells; the cheapest path may be long.
**Greedy fails** — always stepping to the cheaper neighbour can walk into an expensive corner.
**Triangle** — the minimum path from the top of a triangle to the bottom: fill bottom-up.
**Minimum Falling Path Sum** — move down, down-left or down-right.
**Cherry Pickup** — two paths at once: a 3D DP over both walkers' positions.
